# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** 45  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v3 c23 P3](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0003)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>

## Appearance

Lavendar is a petite lady with thick, wavy snow-white hair arranged in puffs and coils. Underneath her white hair, she has a fresh, almost girlish face with pink cheeks, dimples, sweet lips, and soft, wood-brown eyes containing golden glints. She wears dainty gowns, such as cream muslin patterned with pale roses or organdy, which suit her perfectly.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c28 P18](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0018)_

## Personality

Hospitable, sweet, and imaginative, Lavendar enjoys pretending and playing games of imagination even as an adult. She has a voice reminiscent of tinkling water and white satin, and she is a gentle, attentive listener. She keeps a secluded life, but she opens her heart warmly to kindred spirits.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c21 P58](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0058), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c27 P51](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0051)_

## Goals

- reconnect with romantic happiness and companionship  <sub>[v2 c28 P70](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0070), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029)</sub>

## History

Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet life at Echo Lodge, cared for by a series of young Bowman handmaidens, whom she collectively addressed as Charlotta. She struck up a close friendship with Anne Shirley and Diana Barry when they stumbled upon her home, finding a kindred spirit in Anne. Later, after meeting Stephen Irving's young son Paul, Stephen returned to her life after twenty-five years apart. The two reconciled their old romance and were married in an informal outdoor ceremony in her garden at Echo Lodge, afterwards moving together to Boston.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c28 P22](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0022), [v2 c28 P70](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0070), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048)_

## Background by volume

- Named Lavendar by her father because he fell in love with her mother while sleeping in lavender-scented sheets  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Lived at Echo Lodge with her mother until her mother's death ten years prior  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Hired a series of young girls named Charlotta from the Bowman family to live with her for board and clothes  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Engaged to Stephen Irving twenty-five years prior before they quarrelled and parted  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>

## Quotes

> But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you.  <sub>[v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049)</sub>

> But what is the use of being an independent old maid if you can’t be silly when you want to, and when it doesn’t hurt anybody?  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>

> Father named me Lavendar because he was so fond of it.  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>

> Oh, sometimes, I think it is of no use to make friends. They only go out of your life after awhile and leave a hurt that is worse than the emptiness before they came.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>
